tools.name: search_catalog
tools.description: Find software by name, task or recorded filters. Returns at most ten candidates from the same service as native HTML/HTTP search, with recordUrl and met/unmet/unknown requirement assessments. Unknown is not false. No complete profile, publisher fetch, bulk export or functionality guarantee.

q.description: Name or task; at most 512 UTF-8 bytes and 12 words. No model or translation is called.

platform.description: Recorded platform filter, using the HTTP search vocabulary.

category.description: Recorded category slug, including its descendants.

pricing.description: Recorded pricing classification, not proof of a price.

license.description: Recorded license family, not a verified legal conclusion.

require.description: Up to three requirements, e.g. api:true,mcp:true. Not a filter unless unknown is exclude: candidates whose record indicates them are listed first. A requirement is met only with an attributed source, which exists today for api:true and mcp:true (the project's documentation for an API, the official MCP registry for MCP); missing or inferred evidence stays unknown.

unknown.description: Defaults to include candidates needing verification. exclude keeps only candidates with an attributed source for every requirement.

page.description: Same normalization as HTTP search; depth beyond 50 is refused.

limit.description: Same normalization as HTTP search; at most ten combined identities.

tools.name: lookup_project
tools.description: Return the external identifiers PulseGate holds for one project, and for each one how it arrived and whether anyone has checked that it belongs. Also states `brand`: the judged brand the record wears and whether that brand's maker published it (owner), as search_catalog does; null when it wears none. Makes no claim about whether the software is alive, maintained, or working. identity_check is not a confidence scale: nobody_has_checked means no check was ever made, not a weaker yes. caveats on an identifier are short codes, spelled out once at caveats_url. Look up by slug, or by an identifier you already have.

slug.description: The PulseGate slug of the listing.

platform.description: Identifier platform to look up by, e.g. "github_repo" or "npm_package". Use with value.

value.description: The identifier on that platform, e.g. owner/name for github_repo.

tools.name: list_identifier_platforms
tools.description: List every platform PulseGate records identifiers on, with how many identifiers it holds for each. Use it to learn the vocabulary the platform argument of lookup_project accepts.
